chapters.summary: Council staff announces the Committee on Education vote is about to begin, asks attendees to silence electronic devices, and tells them not to approach the dais. Staff then signals Chair Dinowitz that the committee is ready to begin.
chapters.title: Committee staff opens Education Committee vote and instructs attendees to silence devices

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: All right, we'll be starting in a minute.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to today's New York City Council vote for the Committee on Education.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, I would like to remind everyone to silence all electronic devices.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Also, at this point going forward, no one is to approach the days.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair Dinnowitz, we're ready to begin.

chapters.summary: Chair Eric Dinowitz opens the meeting, identifies himself as Chair of the Committee on Education, and welcomes colleagues present. He lists Council Members Gutierrez, Lewis, Zhuang, De La Rosa, Wong, Shulman, and Farias on Zoom.
chapters.title: Chair Dinowitz convenes Education Committee and welcomes attending members

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Eric Dinowitz, Chair of the Committee on Education.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I'd like to welcome and thank you to my colleagues who are present.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: We have Councilmembers Gutierrez, Lewis, Zhuang, De La Rosa, Wong, Shulman, and on Zoom, we have Farias.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz states the committee is voting on two items: Proposed Introduction 853-A, sponsored by Council Member Zhuang, on social and economic factors affecting special education access, and Resolution 650, sponsored by Council Member Gutierrez, opposing the federal Head Start rule change.
chapters.title: Chair Dinowitz announces Intro 853-A and Resolution 650 for committee vote

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Today, the committee is voting on two pieces of legislation.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Proposed Introduction No.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: 853A, sponsored by Councilmember Susan Zhuang, a local law in relation to requiring a study on how social and economic factors affect access to special education programs and services.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And Resolution No.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: 650, sponsored by Councilmember Jennifer Gutierrez, opposing the federally proposed rule change titled

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs, and calling on the federal government to prioritize protecting and growing access to high-quality education for young children.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz details Intro 853-A, which requires DOE to supplement special education reporting with analysis of geographic location, home language, and household income. He notes NYC's large special education system, federal IDEA obligations, a 2023 Comptroller report on missed services, and the bill's requirement to identify barriers and recommend fixes.
chapters.title: Chair Dinowitz explains Intro 853-A special education access study

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Proposed Introduction No.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: 853A requires the DOE to supplement existing special education reporting with analysis on how geographic location, home language, and household income affect students'access to special education programs and services.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: New York City operates the largest special education system in the United States, with approximately 24.2% of K-12 students in the 2025-2026 school year having been classified as having a disability.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Under federal law, students with disabilities are entitled to a free and appropriate education in the least restrictive environment, as guaranteed.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: by the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Yet, a 2023 New York City Comptroller report found that the DOE failed to deliver mandated special education services to thousands of students.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Proposed Introduction 853A aims to enhance DOE's reporting on the delivery of special education services.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: So students and families can better understand the impact of social and economic factors on access to those services.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: The legislation also requires DUE to identify any barriers to access to special education programs and services and requires DUE to make recommendations on how to address those barriers.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: As a council member, but more importantly, as a former special education teacher, I am proud to support this bill as a co-sponsor and want to thank Council Member Zwayne for moving this bill forward.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz describes Resolution 650, which opposes the federal proposed rule 'Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs.' He says the rule would weaken standards, allow larger classes, reduce teacher qualifications, cut health and family supports, and restrict non-English instruction, potentially harming vulnerable children.
chapters.title: Chair Dinowitz explains Resolution 650 opposing Head Start rule change

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Resolution 650 opposes the federally proposed rule change titled Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: The proposed rule change would remove or weaken many of the standards that currently govern Head Start, allowing larger class sizes, reducing teacher qualification requirements,

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: cutting certain health and family support requirements, and restricting instruction in languages other than English.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Research has found that Head Start prepares young children for school,

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: and over time increases educational attainment.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: The proposed changes could lower the quality and safety of early childhood education for thousands of New York children, the thousands that could

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: currently benefit from Head Start, especially for vulnerable students by reducing individual attention, specialized support, and access to bilingual learning.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember Gutierrez, for this resolution.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz thanks his staff and Education Committee staff, including counsel and policy analysts, for preparing the vote. He then turns the meeting over to the clerk to conduct the roll call.
chapters.title: Chair Dinowitz thanks committee staff and turns to clerk for roll call

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I'd like to thank my staff, Theo Solter and Jenna Klaus, and the Education Committee staff, Senior Counsel Alejandro Carvajal, Senior Policy Analyst Chloe Rivera, and Policy Analyst Katie Salina,

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: as well as Principal Financial Analyst Andrew Lane Lawless, Senior Financial Analyst Grace Amato, and Financial Fellow Emily Sosa for preparing today's vote.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I will now turn to the clerk for the roll.

summary: The Committee on Education met to vote on Intro 853-A, a special education access study bill, and Resolution 650 opposing the federal Head Start rule change.
Chair Eric Dinowitz explained both items, then the clerk conducted a roll call that was held open for late-arriving members.
Intro 853-A passed 11-0 and Resolution 650 passed 10-1, with Council Member Phil Wong voting nay on the resolution; the meeting adjourned.
title: Committee on Education
topic: Requiring a study on how social and economic factors affect access to special education programs and services
